correctness.rationale: For an A-vertex facing j zeros, its only fixed action is 1 if its threshold is at most j and 0 if its threshold is at least j+2; at j+1 neither action is fixed. Apply the same test on B to obtain the two count equations, both vetoes and uniqueness for each pair. As i increases between distinct solutions, j must strictly decrease by monotonicity and the two count equations. A vertex switching on each side gives both gaps at least two, including at the endpoints. All thresholds 1 give no solution; paired even thresholds 2,2,...,2r,2r with remaining thresholds 0 force precisely (2t,2r-2t), 0≤t≤r. This also checks the r=0 case and nonconstant rules in the even balanced case. Clipping above opposite size + 2 preserves the veto and suffix tests, and there is one candidate per i. The three stated finite workload totals independently sum to 19,432, 1,111,428 and 1,010. The uploaded code was read, not executed; its finite range omits the constant-zero category but the proof covers it.
